rock.why: A keeps glowing fissures that light their stone, glowing world-tinted pools and a clear hue per world. B removes the glow and light spill, turns pools into flat off-palette cubes, and blurs CRYOS into MAELIS.

lighting.why: A keeps glowing emissives, light that spills from lava and fissures onto stone, and a distinct hue per world. B flattens all of that into unlit decals and matte tiles, and mixes up the world palettes (green Cryos, violet Maelis).

identity.why: B keeps each world's hue at every depth and in every core. A goes neutral at mid depth and swaps the CRYOS and MAELIS palettes (green CRYOS, violet MAELIS), so its deeper frames misidentify the world.

fluids.why: B turns fluids into cohesive, world-hued glowing pools and makes fissures light their stone as in 04. A's flat green/orange tiles and unlit hairline fissures miss every reference. Both still fail to make the core flood its chamber.

characters.why: The pod and pilot are identical in A and B. A edges ahead because the pilot sits in warm, lit vault masonry and the scenes around the creatures carry more light. B only wins on a more readable stillwalker silhouette.

vaults.why: B adds a cool masonry backdrop with warm lantern pools, and its lit fangs make the hazards far more legible. That moves it clearly toward the 08-vault references, at a small cost: dark footing contrasts less against the wall in Return and Kindled.

ui.why: The only UI difference is the ore icons: B's are cleaner, more distinct silhouettes that sit in the amber VEIL palette, while A's are muddy (the gold has a dark overlay) and its teal copper clashes. Everything else is identical, so the margin is small.

minerals.why: B delivers glow, colour identity and the brief's silhouettes for almost every ore, and gives the mimic a fair tell. A is flat, unlit and mis-coloured, and several pairs are confusable. B's remaining problems are square-clipped halos, converging pale halos and iron's low visibility.
